questions.questionText: A person travels from A to B at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances = Harmonic mean = 2xy / (x + y) = 2(40)(60) / (40 + 60) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h.

questions.questionText: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 20 minutes late. What is his usual time to cover the distance?
questions.explanation: Speed becomes 3/4, so time becomes 4/3 of usual time. Extra time = 4/3 T - T = 1/3 T = 20 minutes => Usual time T = 60 minutes.

questions.questionText: If a student walks at 4 km/h from his house, he reaches school 5 minutes late. If he walks at 5 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance between his house and school?
questions.explanation: Difference in time = 5 - (-10) = 15 minutes = 1/4 hour. Distance D = [s1 * s2 / (s2 - s1)] * Δt = [4 * 5 / (5 - 4)] * (1/4) = 20 * (1/4) = 5 km.

questions.questionText: Two trains leave stations A and B, 450 km apart, at the same time and travel towards each other at 50 km/h and 40 km/h respectively. After how many hours will they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50 + 40 = 90 km/h. Time to meet = Total distance / Relative speed = 450 / 90 = 5 hours.

questions.questionText: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 54 km/h and including stoppages, it is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.explanation: Stoppage time per hour = [(Speed without - Speed with) / Speed without] * 60 = [(54 - 45) / 54] * 60 = (9 / 54) * 60 = 10 minutes.

questions.questionText: Two persons start at the same time from points A and B towards each other. After crossing each other, they take 4 hours and 9 hours respectively to reach B and A. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanation: Formula: S1 / S2 = √(t2 / t1) = √(9 / 4) = 3 / 2. Speed ratio is 3 : 2.

questions.questionText: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m and B beats C by 100 m. By how many meters does A beat C in the same race?
questions.explanation: When A runs 1000 m, B runs 900 m. When B runs 1000 m, C runs 900 m => When B runs 900 m, C runs 900 * (900/1000) = 810 m. So when A runs 1000 m, C runs 810 m. A beats C by 1000 - 810 = 190 m.

questions.questionText: A man covers a certain distance on car. Had he moved 4 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 minutes less. If he had moved 2 km/h slower, he would have taken 20 minutes more. Find the distance.
questions.explanation: Let speed be S and time be T. D = S*T. D = (S + 4)(T - 1/2) => 4T - S/2 - 2 = 0 => 8T - S = 4. D = (S - 2)(T + 1/3) => -2T + S/3 - 2/3 = 0 => -6T + S = 2. Adding equations: 2T = 6 => T = 3 hours. S = 8(3) - 4 = 20 km/h. Distance = 20 * 3 = 60 km.

questions.questionText: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 10 km/h and that of the policeman is 11 km/h, what is the distance between them after 6 minutes?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 11 - 10 = 1 km/h = 1000 m / 60 min = 50/3 m/min. Distance covered in 6 minutes = (50/3) * 6 = 100 m. Remaining distance = 200 - 100 = 100 m.

questions.questionText: A man rides a bicycle at 10 km/h for 2 hours and then walks at 4 km/h for 3 hours. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 10 * 2 + 4 * 3 = 20 + 12 = 32 km. Total time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours. Average speed = 32 / 5 = 6.4 km/h.

questions.questionText: A circular track has a circumference of 600 m. A and B start simultaneously from the same point in the same direction at speeds of 15 m/s and 10 m/s. When will they first meet at the starting point?
questions.explanation: Time for 1 round: A = 600/15 = 40 s, B = 600/10 = 60 s. Meeting at starting point = LCM(40, 60) = 120 seconds.

questions.questionText: A car travels a distance of 170 km in 2 hours. What is its speed in meters per second?
In a 100 m race, A can give B a start of 20 m and C a start of 28 m. In a race of 500 m, how much start can B give C?
questions.explanation: When A runs 100 m, B runs 80 m and C runs 72 m. Ratio B : C = 80 : 72 = 10 : 9. In a 500 m race, when B runs 500 m, C runs 500 * (9/10) = 450 m. B can give C a start of 500 - 450 = 50 m.

questions.questionText: A person travels equal distances at speeds of 10 km/h, 20 km/h, and 30 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?

A monkey climbs 30 feet up a greased pole in the first minute and slips down 15 feet in the next minute. If the pole is 105 feet high, in how many minutes will the monkey reach the top for the first time?
questions.explanation: Net climb in 2 minutes = 30 - 15 = 15 feet. Target before final jump = 105 - 30 = 75 feet. Time for 75 feet = (75 / 15) * 2 = 10 minutes. In minute 11, the monkey climbs 30 feet, reaching 75 + 30 = 105 feet (top). Total time = 11 minutes.

questions.questionText: A train travels from P to Q at a speed of 35 km/h and returns at a speed of 45 km/h. Find the average speed of the train.
A car covers 4 successive 3 km stretches at speeds of 10 km/h, 20 km/h, 30 km/h, and 60 km/h respectively. Its average speed is:
An aeroplane covers a certain distance at a speed of 240 km/h in 5 hours. To cover the same distance in 1 2/3 hours, it must travel at a speed of:
questions.explanation: Distance = 240 * 5 = 1200 km. Time = 5/3 hours. Required speed = 1200 / (5/3) = 1200 * (3/5) = 720 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two boys start at the same time from two points 30 km apart towards each other at 4 km/h and 6 km/h. A fly sitting on one boy's shoulder flies towards the other at 15 km/h, turns back on reaching, and continues flying back and forth until the boys meet. What is the total distance covered by the fly?
questions.explanation: Time until the boys meet = 30 / (4 + 6) = 3 hours. Distance covered by fly = Fly speed * Time = 15 * 3 = 45 km.

questions.questionText: A man walked at 5 km/h for 4 hours and ran at 10 km/h for 2 hours. Find his average speed for the entire journey.
questions.explanation: Total distance = 5*4 + 10*2 = 20 + 20 = 40 km. Total time = 4 + 2 = 6 hours. Average speed = 40 / 6 = 6.67 km/h.

questions.questionText: A person crosses a 600 m long street in 5 minutes. What is his speed in km/h?
An express train travels at an average speed of 100 km/h, stopping for 3 minutes after every 75 km. How long will it take to reach its destination 600 km away?
questions.explanation: Running time = 600 / 100 = 6 hours. Number of stoppages = 600 / 75 - 1 = 8 - 1 = 7 stoppages (no stoppage at final destination). Total stoppage time = 7 * 3 = 21 minutes. Total time = 6 hours 21 minutes.

questions.questionText: A man walking at 6 km/h reaches his destination 20 minutes late. If he walks at 7 km/h, he is late by 5 minutes. What is the distance to his destination?
questions.explanation: Time difference = 20 - 5 = 15 minutes = 1/4 hour. Distance = [6 * 7 / (7 - 6)] * (1/4) = 42 * (1/4) = 10.5 km.

questions.questionText: Two runners A and B run on a 400 m circular track. Their speeds are 20 m/s and 16 m/s. If they run in opposite directions, after how much time will they first meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 20 + 16 = 36 m/s. Time to meet = 400 / 36 = 100 / 9 = 11.11 seconds.

questions.questionText: A man covers a distance in 50 minutes if he runs at a speed of 48 km/h. At what speed must he run to reduce the time of journey to 40 minutes?
A and B run a 1 km race. A gives B a start of 50 m and still beats him by 10 seconds. If A's speed is 5 m/s, what is B's speed?
questions.explanation: Time for A to run 1000 m = 1000 / 5 = 200 seconds. B runs (1000 - 50) = 950 m in (200 + 10) = 210 seconds. B's speed = 950 / 210 = 95 / 21 = 4.52 m/s.

questions.questionText: A car covers 1/3 of its journey at 20 km/h, another 1/3 at 30 km/h, and the last 1/3 at 60 km/h. What is the average speed of the car?
A policeman chases a thief who has 100 m head start. The policeman runs 1 km in 8 minutes and the thief runs 1 km in 10 minutes. How far will the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: Policeman speed = 1000 / 480 = 25/12 m/s. Thief speed = 1000 / 600 = 5/3 = 20/12 m/s. Relative speed = 5/12 m/s. Time to overtake = 100 / (5/12) = 240 seconds. Distance run by thief = (5/3) * 240 = 400 m.

questions.questionText: If a person walks at 14 km/h instead of 10 km/h, he would have walked 20 km more. What was the actual distance travelled by him?
A motorist travels to a place 150 km away at an average speed of 50 km/h and returns at 30 km/h. His average speed for the whole journey in km/h is:
A man can reach a certain place in 30 hours. If he reduces his speed by 1/15th, he goes 10 km less in that time. Find his speed.
questions.explanation: Reduction in speed = S/15. In 30 hours, distance lost = 30 * (S/15) = 2S = 10 km => S = 5 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two trains start simultaneously from Delhi and Jaipur and proceed towards each other at 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, the second train has travelled 180 km more than the first. What is the distance between Delhi and Jaipur?
questions.explanation: Speed difference = 95 - 80 = 15 km/h. Time taken to meet = 180 / 15 = 12 hours. Total distance = Sum of speeds * Time = (80 + 95) * 12 = 175 * 12 = 2,100 km.

questions.questionText: A man travels 35 km partly at 4 km/h and partly at 5 km/h. If he covers the former distance at 5 km/h and latter at 4 km/h, he could cover 2 km more in the same time. What was the time taken in the first case?
questions.explanation: Let distance at 4 km/h be x, at 5 km/h be y. x + y = 35. Time T1 = x/4 + y/5. Swapped: y/4 + x/5 = T1. Distance covered = 37 km. x/4 + y/5 = T => 5x + 4y = 20T. Also 4x + 5y = 20T. Solving gives T = 8 hours.

questions.questionText: In a 500 m race, the ratio of speeds of two contestants A and B is 3 : 4. A has a start of 140 m. Then A wins by:
questions.explanation: A has to run 500 - 140 = 360 m. When A runs 360 m, B runs 360 * (4/3) = 480 m. Since B only reaches 480 m when A finishes 500 m, A wins by 500 - 480 = 20 m.

questions.questionText: A car travels at 25 km/h for the first half of a total distance and at 50 km/h for the second half. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
A man covered a distance of 61 km in 9 hours. He traveled partly on foot at 4 km/h and partly on bicycle at 9 km/h. What distance did he travel on foot?
questions.explanation: Let foot time be t. 4t + 9(9 - t) = 61 => 4t + 81 - 9t = 61 => -5t = -20 => t = 4 hours. Distance on foot = 4 * 4 = 16 km.

questions.questionText: A train covers a distance of 10 km in 12 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 5 km/h, what is the time taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.explanation: Original speed = 10 / (12/60) = 50 km/h. Reduced speed = 50 - 5 = 45 km/h. New time = 10 / 45 hours = (10/45) * 60 = 40/3 mins = 13 min 20 sec.

questions.questionText: A boy goes to school with a speed of 3 km/h and returns with a speed of 2 km/h. If he takes 5 hours in all, what is the distance in km between his village and school?
questions.explanation: Total Time = D/3 + D/2 = 5 => 5D / 6 = 5 => D = 6 km.

questions.questionText: Two cyclists start from the same point at the same time and move in opposite directions at 15 km/h and 20 km/h. After how many hours will they be 140 km apart?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 15 + 20 = 35 km/h. Time = 140 / 35 = 4 hours.

questions.questionText: A person travels from A to B at 20 km/h and from B to C at 30 km/h. If AB = BC, find the average speed for the whole journey from A to C.
A car covers a distance of 715 km at a constant speed. If the speed had been 10 km/h more, the journey would have taken 2 hours less. What is the original speed of the car?
A man can travel 120 km in 6 hours. If he travels 1/3 of the distance at 40 km/h, at what speed must he travel the remaining distance to finish on time?
questions.explanation: 1/3 distance = 40 km. Time for first part = 40 / 40 = 1 hour. Remaining distance = 80 km. Remaining time = 6 - 1 = 5 hours. Required speed = 80 / 5 = 16 km/h.

questions.questionText: Walking at 6/7 of his normal speed, a man is 12 minutes late. What is his usual time to cover the distance?
questions.explanation: Time becomes 7/6 of usual. 7/6 T - T = 1/6 T = 12 mins => T = 72 minutes (1 hr 12 mins).

questions.questionText: Two cars A and B start from two points P and Q, 120 km apart, towards each other at 9:00 AM. If their speeds are 40 km/h and 20 km/h, at what time will they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 40 + 20 = 60 km/h. Time taken = 120 / 60 = 2 hours. Meeting time = 9:00 AM + 2 hours = 11:00 AM.

questions.questionText: A runner completes a 400 m lap in 50 seconds. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.concept: Lap Speed to Metric Hourly Rate

questions.questionText: If a car travels at 80 km/h, it reaches its destination 10 minutes early. If it travels at 60 km/h, it reaches 10 minutes late. Find the distance.
In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and C by 13 m. In a race of 180 m, by how many meters will B beat C?
questions.explanation: When A runs 100 m, B runs 90 m and C runs 87 m. When B runs 90 m, C runs 87 m (ratio C/B = 87/90 = 29/30). In a 180 m race, when B runs 180 m, C runs 180 * (29/30) = 174 m. B beats C by 180 - 174 = 6 m.

questions.questionText: A thief steals a car at 1:30 PM and drives it at 40 km/h. The theft is discovered at 2:00 PM and the owner sets off in another car at 50 km/h. At what time will he overtake the thief?
questions.explanation: In 30 minutes (1/2 hour), thief covers 40 * 0.5 = 20 km. Relative speed = 50 - 40 = 10 km/h. Time to overtake = 20 / 10 = 2 hours. Overtake time = 2:00 PM + 2 hours = 4:00 PM.

questions.questionText: A man covers a distance of 150 km in 3 hours. He travels the first 60 km at 30 km/h. What was his speed for the rest of the journey?
questions.explanation: Time for first 60 km = 60 / 30 = 2 hours. Remaining distance = 150 - 60 = 90 km. Remaining time = 3 - 2 = 1 hour. Speed for rest = 90 / 1 = 90 km/h.

questions.questionText: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 7 : 8. If the second train runs 400 km in 4 hours, then the speed of the first train is:
questions.explanation: Speed of 2nd train = 400 / 4 = 100 km/h. 8 parts = 100 km/h => 1 part = 12.5 km/h. Speed of 1st train = 7 * 12.5 = 87.5 km/h.

questions.questionText: A circular race track has length 800 m. Two cyclists start from the same point in the same direction at 12 m/s and 20 m/s. When will they first cross each other anywhere on the track?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 20 - 12 = 8 m/s. First crossing = Track length / Relative speed = 800 / 8 = 100 seconds.

questions.questionText: A person walks from station P to station Q at 5 km/h and returns by cycling at 15 km/h. What is his average speed for the round trip?
If John walks at 3 km/h, he misses a train by 2 minutes. If he walks at 4 km/h, he reaches the station 2 minutes before the train leaves. How far is the station from his house?
A car covers 120 km in 2 hours and another 180 km in 3 hours. Find the average speed of the car for the entire 300 km journey.
questions.explanation: Total distance = 120 + 180 = 300 km. Total time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours. Average speed = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.

questions.questionText: Two persons A and B start from two places 24 km apart. A walks at 4 km/h and B at 2 km/h in the same direction. In how many hours will A overtake B?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 4 - 2 = 2 km/h. Time to overtake = 24 / 2 = 12 hours.

questions.questionText: A car completes a journey in 10 hours. It covers the first half of the distance at 21 km/h and the second half at 24 km/h. What is the total distance covered in km?
questions.explanation: Let total distance be 2D. D/21 + D/24 = 10 => (8D + 7D)/168 = 10 => 15D / 168 = 10 => 15D = 1680 => D = 112 km. Total distance = 2D = 224 km.

questions.questionText: A motor cyclist travels from his house to town at 32 km/h and arrives 5 minutes late. If he travels at 40 km/h, he arrives 5 minutes early. Find the distance to town.

An escalator moves up at 2 steps per second. A person walks up the moving escalator and takes 20 seconds to reach the top. If he walks at 3 steps per second relative to the escalator, how many steps are visible on the escalator?
questions.explanation: Total effective speed = 3 + 2 = 5 steps/sec. Visible steps = Effective speed * Time = 5 * 20 = 100 steps.

questions.questionText: A cyclist covers 500 m in 2 minutes. What is his speed in km/h?
A person travels 285 km in 6 hours in two stages. In the first stage, he travels by bus at 40 km/h. In the second stage, he travels by train at 55 km/h. How much distance did he travel by train?
questions.explanation: Let train time be t. 40(6 - t) + 55t = 285 => 240 - 40t + 55t = 285 => 15t = 45 => t = 3 hours. Distance by train = 55 * 3 = 165 km.
